title: Distinct Prime Factors of Product of Array
summary: For an array of positive integers, determine the count of unique prime factors present in their product, considering a prime number as divisible only by 1 and itself, and a factor as an integer that divides another without a remainder.
statement: For an array of positive integers, determine the count of unique prime factors present in their product, considering a prime number as divisible only by 1 and itself, and a factor as an integer that divides another without a remainder.
constraints: Every array value is an integer from 2 through 1000.
A prime contributes once if it divides the product of all values, regardless of exponent.
Return the number of distinct contributing primes.
hints: A prime divides the total product exactly when it divides at least one array value.
Factor each number independently and insert discovered primes into one shared set.
After dividing out each small factor completely, add any residual value greater than one.
Trial division finds every prime factor, and the set removes repetitions within and across numbers.
editorial: Trial division finds every prime factor, and the set removes repetitions within and across numbers.

tests.explanation: The product has exactly the prime factors 2, 3, 5, and 7.
Every value contains only prime factor two, so the distinct count is one.
